```text
The support-subset proof exposed a real landing-surface mismatch before any
Lean theorem was forced:

  audit payload term index n
  != Lean PrimeShiftIndexL3 index n

The audit enumerates prime powers grouped by prime:
  (2,1), (2,2), ..., (3,1), ...

Lean's active dictionary is ordered by the existing `activeL3PrimeBaseEntry`

  audit n=8 has shift log 3
  Lean n=8 is base 13, exponent 1

the generated module compiled.
```

```text
terms are remapped by `(prime base, exponent)` from audit order into Lean
`PrimeShiftIndexL3` order before emitting midpoint/radius tables and declared
support sets.

  same PrimeCert lower/upper log bounds that Lean has available.
```

There is no fixed explicit `C0/C1` theorem currently wired into this Step33
gate.

Numerical diagnostic only, not a Lean proof: unfolding the current
four-sinc-power tail formula gives approximately:

```text
primary left  ~= 6.754599227815916  * (C0 + C1)
control left  ~= 3.5728561233686142 * (C0 + C1)

primary common tail radius ~= 1.329645459799433e-18
control common tail radius ~= 8.231371264417030e-17

required primary: C0 + C1 <= 1.968503851899694e-19
required control: C0 + C1 <= 2.303863066463534e-17
```

So the existing `TailGrowthBound` receiver is much too coarse for the generated
common tail radii.  This is not an `ARadius` or CSV issue.

I also checked the obvious stronger absolute-value variants.  Keeping the full
available sinc power but still using global linear growth would require roughly
`C0 + C1 <= 0.039` in both primary/control.  A tail-constant absolute bound on
`|a_star t|` for `t >= 260` would need roughly:

```text
sup_{t >= 260} |a_star t| <= 10.68
```

DLMF 5.11 gives the standard digamma asymptotic `psi(z) ~ log z`, which on
`z = 1/4 + i*pi*t` predicts `|a_star t|` on this tail at the scale of
`2*pi*log t`, around `35` already near `t=260`.  Therefore a pure absolute
tail majorant is the wrong proof shape for these generated tail radii; the
remaining A-tail certificate must exploit oscillation/cancellation or use a
proof-producing tail interval generator.

```lean

RawOmegaAChunkIntegral.RawOmegaATaylorModelCertificate.setIntegral_Ioc_polynomial_of_le

RawOmegaAChunkIntegral.RawOmegaATaylorModelCertificate.setIntegral_Ioc_upperModel_of_le

RawOmegaAChunkIntegral.RawOmegaATaylorModelCertificate.Valid.controlK9_of_model_integral_bounds
```

Meaning:

```text
Lean now computes the integral of the rational Taylor polynomial as a finite
endpoint power sum:
  integral (sum_i c_i * (eta - center)^i)
  = sum_i c_i * ((U-center)^(i+1) - (L-center)^(i+1))/(i+1).

The lower/upper model integrals are then:
  polynomialIntegral - (U-L) * remainder
  polynomialIntegral + (U-L) * remainder.
```

The generated payload no longer has to prove semantic inequalities involving
`∫ lowerModel` and `∫ upperModel`; it can prove endpoint-form inequalities:

```text
chunkLower <= lowerModelIntegral
upperModelIntegral <= chunkUpper
```
